deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.citation: Rizer NW, Klein E, Copenhaver MS, Zhao X, Kelen GD, Hinson JS (2026) Early Clinical Deterioration Among Emergency Department Boarders: A Retrospective Analysis, Ann Emerg Med 87(6):681-693 (abstract): of 173,168 floor-level medical admissions boarding 4-48 h at five hospitals, 6,299 (3.6%) escalated to intermediate or intensive care within 48 h of the admission order, 2,823 (45%) of them while still in the ED; median boarding 12.5 h (IQR 8.2-20.7) with deterioration vs 10.2 h without; +0.8% relative risk overall and +2.4% for in-ED deterioration per extra boarding hour; 28-day mortality 13.0% after deterioration vs 3.9%.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.note: DERIVED by the research agent for ESI 2 and 3 only: 3.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0029 per hour (ESI 2 value 0.003); in-ED events only, 1.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0013 (low end); ESI 3 set to a third of ESI 2 because most ESI 3 patients are discharged. The source measures admitted patients boarding after treatment, not untreated patients in the waiting room; no waiting-room deterioration rate was found. ESI 1, 4 and 5 values are unchanged Wave 0 placeholders and remain ASSUMED. US academic system, 2018-2024.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): only the ESI 2 value is computed from the cited source; ESI 3 is an assumed fraction of it; ESI 1, 4 and 5 are ASSUMED placeholders.

death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.citation: Derived from (a) Singer AJ et al. (2011) Acad Emerg Med, 41,256 admissions: in-hospital mortality 2.5% boarded <2 h vs 4.5% boarded >=12 h (about 0.0017 per hour); (b) Jones S et al. (2022) Emerg Med J, 5.25 million admitted patients, England: 30-day mortality rises linearly from 5 to 12 h after arrival, one extra death per 82 patients delayed beyond 6-8 h; (c) Guttmann A et al. (2011) BMJ, 13.9 million discharged patients, Ontario: 8,502 deaths among 6.64 million high-acuity and 1,998 among 7.29 million low-acuity discharged patients within 7 days, and one hour less mean stay estimated to avoid 6.5% and 12.7% of them (about 8e-5 and 4e-5 per patient-hour). ESI 2 = admitted-patient figure; ESI 3 = 30% admitted-type + 70% discharged high-acuity; ESI 4-5 = discharged low-acuity.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.note: DERIVED by the research agent; observational, confounded, and these are attributable deaths within 7 to 30 days per hour of delay, not deaths inside the department. ESI 1 (0.01) has no usable source and remains ASSUMED: ESI 1 patients are treated immediately by definition. Other URLs: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1553-2712.2011.01236.x (Singer), https://doi.org/10.1136/emermed-2021-211572 (Jones). In Jones the effect starts about 5 h after arrival; applying the hazard from minute zero overstates harm for short waits.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): the ESI 1 value is an ASSUMED placeholder; ESI 2-5 are derived from the cited sources.

lwbs_patience_min.citation: Batt RJ, Terwiesch C (2015) Waiting Patiently: An Empirical Study of Queue Abandonment in an Emergency Department, Management Science 61(1):39-59 (working-paper PDF read). Table 1: mean wait 1.0/1.9/1.3/1.3 h and LWBS 1.7%/9.5%/4.7%/7.4% for ESI 2/3/4/5 (N = 27,538/65,773/39,878/10,509); 'ESI 1 patients ... do not abandon'. Values are the exponential mean patience that reproduces each LWBS share at that mean wait: theta = -wait / ln(1 - LWBS), rounded.
lwbs_patience_min.note: DERIVED by the research agent from a published table, not a published estimate. One US urban academic ED, about 180,000 visits. ESI 1 is set effectively infinite (they did not leave). The same paper's regression gives about +0.5 percentage points LWBS per extra 15 min of wait for ESI 3 (hazard about 0.02/h, mean 3,000 min), hence the wide range. Patience also falls with visible queue length (one more person in the waiting room = +0.5 points). The Wave 0 placeholder (240 min for ESI 3) would give about 38% LWBS at a 1.9 h wait, four times the observed 9.5%.

boarding_los_penalty.unit: fraction of inpatient LOS per boarding hour
boarding_los_penalty.citation: Singer AJ, Thode HC, Viccellio P, Pines JM (2011) The association between length of emergency department boarding and mortality, Acad Emerg Med 18(12): mean hospital stay 5.6 days when boarded <2 h vs 8.7 days when boarded >24 h (41,256 admissions, one US academic ED, unadjusted) = at most about +2.3% of stay per boarding hour. Roussel M et al. (2023) JAMA Intern Med: patients aged 75+ who spent the night in the ED had length-of-stay rate ratio 1.20 (1.11-1.31). Sun BC et al. (2013) Ann Emerg Med: admission on a high-crowding day = +0.8% length of stay (995,379 admissions, adjusted).
boarding_los_penalty.note: Loose range; value set inside it. The unadjusted single-site figure (0.023) is the ceiling because sicker patients board longer; the adjusted multi-hospital figure is far smaller. US and France.

(2022) Emerg Med J, 5.25 million admitted patients, England: 30-day mortality rises linearly from 5 to 12 h after arrival, one extra death per 82 patients delayed beyond 6-8 h; (c) Guttmann A et al. (2011) BMJ, 13.9 million discharged patients, Ontario: 8,502 deaths among 6.64 million high-acuity and 1,998 among 7.29 million low-acuity discharged patients within 7 days, and one hour less mean stay estimated to avoid 6.5% and 12.7% of them (about 8e-5 and 4e-5 per patient-hour). ESI 2 = admitted-patient figure; ESI 3 = 30% admitted-type + 70% discharged high-acuity; ESI 4-5 = discharged low-acuity.

Other URLs: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1553-2712.2011.01236.x (Singer), https://doi.org/10.1136/emermed-2021-211572 (Jones). inpatient_revenue.citation: CMS IPPS FY 2027 final rule + correction notice: Tables 1A/1D standardized amounts (labor 4519.68, nonlabor 2328.32, capital 539.95) and Impact File row for CCN 310038 (wage index 1.2727, teaching factor 0.18135, DSH factor 0.04234, capital GAF 1.1795501088188711, transfer-adjusted case-mix index 2.461, uncompensated-care amount per claim 1847.02); operating = (labor*wage_index + nonlabor) * (1 + TCHOP + DSHOPP); capital = capital_rate * GAF * (1 + TCHCP + DSHCPP); payment(weight) = (operating + capital) * weight + UCP per claim. Outliers, VBP/readmission/HAC adjustments, new-technology add-ons and transfers ignored.

BASE-RATE ASSUMPTION: the stay is paid at this hospital's average Medicare case-mix index (2.461, all Medicare discharges including transplant and cardiac surgery); medical admissions through the ED are on average lighter, so this is an upper estimate - lower end of range = a DRG weight of 1.0 (12492 usd). Payment per unit of DRG weight = 10645 usd. Cross-check: the hospital's FY2024 cost report gives net patient revenue 1,665,310,131 usd x inpatient share of charges 0.689 / 36,561 discharges = about 31,400 usd per discharge, all payers. deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.citation: Rizer NW, Klein E, Copenhaver MS, Zhao X, Kelen GD, Hinson JS (2026) Early Clinical Deterioration Among Emergency Department Boarders: A Retrospective Analysis, Ann Emerg Med 87(6):681-693 (abstract): of 173,168 floor-level medical admissions boarding 4-48 h at five hospitals, 6,299 (3.6%) escalated to intermediate or intensive care within 48 h of the admission order, 2,823 (45%) of them while still in the ED; median boarding 12.5 h (IQR 8.2-20.7) with deterioration vs 10.2 h without; +0.8% relative risk overall and +2.4% for in-ED deterioration per extra boarding hour; 28-day mortality 13.0% after deterioration vs 3.9%.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.note: DERIVED by the research agent for ESI 2 and 3 only: 3.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0029 per hour (ESI 2 value 0.003); in-ED events only, 1.6% / 12.5 h = 0.0013 (low end); ESI 3 set to a third of ESI 2 because most ESI 3 patients are discharged. The source measures admitted patients boarding after treatment, not untreated patients in the waiting room; no waiting-room deterioration rate was found. ESI 1, 4 and 5 values are unchanged Wave 0 placeholders and remain ASSUMED. US academic system, 2018-2024.
deterioration_hazard_per_hour_waiting.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): only the ESI 2 value is computed from the cited source; ESI 3 is an assumed fraction of it; ESI 1, 4 and 5 are ASSUMED placeholders.

death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.citation: Derived from (a) Singer AJ et al. (2011) Acad Emerg Med, 41,256 admissions: in-hospital mortality 2.5% boarded <2 h vs 4.5% boarded >=12 h (about 0.0017 per hour); (b) Jones S et al. (2022) Emerg Med J, 5.25 million admitted patients, England: 30-day mortality rises linearly from 5 to 12 h after arrival, one extra death per 82 patients delayed beyond 6-8 h; (c) Guttmann A et al. (2011) BMJ, 13.9 million discharged patients, Ontario: 8,502 deaths among 6.64 million high-acuity and 1,998 among 7.29 million low-acuity discharged patients within 7 days, and one hour less mean stay estimated to avoid 6.5% and 12.7% of them (about 8e-5 and 4e-5 per patient-hour). ESI 2 = admitted-patient figure; ESI 3 = 30% admitted-type + 70% discharged high-acuity; ESI 4-5 = discharged low-acuity.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.note: DERIVED by the research agent; observational, confounded, and these are attributable deaths within 7 to 30 days per hour of delay, not deaths inside the department. ESI 1 (0.01) has no usable source and remains ASSUMED: ESI 1 patients are treated immediately by definition. Other URLs: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1553-2712.2011.01236.x (Singer), https://doi.org/10.1136/emermed-2021-211572 (Jones). In Jones the effect starts about 5 h after arrival; applying the hazard from minute zero overstates harm for short waits.
death_hazard_per_hour_untreated.mixed_provenance: PER-ELEMENT PROVENANCE (audit 2026-10-10): the ESI 1 value is an ASSUMED placeholder; ESI 2-5 are derived from the cited sources.

lwbs_patience_min.citation: Batt RJ, Terwiesch C (2015) Waiting Patiently: An Empirical Study of Queue Abandonment in an Emergency Department, Management Science 61(1):39-59 (working-paper PDF read). Table 1: mean wait 1.0/1.9/1.3/1.3 h and LWBS 1.7%/9.5%/4.7%/7.4% for ESI 2/3/4/5 (N = 27,538/65,773/39,878/10,509); 'ESI 1 patients ... do not abandon'. Values are the exponential mean patience that reproduces each LWBS share at that mean wait: theta = -wait / ln(1 - LWBS), rounded.
lwbs_patience_min.note: DERIVED by the research agent from a published table, not a published estimate. One US urban academic ED, about 180,000 visits. ESI 1 is set effectively infinite (they did not leave). The same paper's regression gives about +0.5 percentage points LWBS per extra 15 min of wait for ESI 3 (hazard about 0.02/h, mean 3,000 min), hence the wide range. Patience also falls with visible queue length (one more person in the waiting room = +0.5 points). The Wave 0 placeholder (240 min for ESI 3) would give about 38% LWBS at a 1.9 h wait, four times the observed 9.5%.

boarding_los_penalty.unit: fraction of inpatient LOS per boarding hour

Roussel M et al. (2023) JAMA Intern Med: patients aged 75+ who spent the night in the ED had length-of-stay rate ratio 1.20 (1.11-1.31). Sun BC et al. (2013) Ann Emerg Med: admission on a high-crowding day = +0.8% length of stay (995,379 admissions, adjusted).
boarding_los_penalty.note: Loose range; value set inside it. The unadjusted single-site figure (0.023) is the ceiling because sicker patients board longer; the adjusted multi-hospital figure is far smaller. US and France.

fatigue_error_multiplier.citation: Landrigan CP et al. (2004) Effect of reducing interns' work hours on serious medical errors in intensive care units, N Engl J Med 351:1838-48 (randomised; 2,203 patient-days): 35.9% more serious medical errors on the traditional schedule with 24 h+ shifts (136.0 vs 100.1 per 1,000 patient-days), 5.6 times as many serious diagnostic errors. (2006) PLoS Med 3(12):e487 (2,737 interns, 17,003 monthly reports, self-report): odds ratio 3.5 (3.3-3.7) of a fatigue-related significant medical error in months with 1-4 extended shifts and 7.5 with 5 or more.

(2004) Health Aff 23(4):202-12 found error risk significantly higher past 12 h, with overtime and past 40 h/week (393 nurses, 5,317 shifts; effect size not in the abstract). procedure_min.note: DERIVED lognormal: median 51.1 and IQR 41.1-65.0 give sigma 0.34 (cv 0.35) and mean 54. Netherlands (one university hospital) and France (one ED). arrival_multiplier.citation: CDC FluView, Weekly US Influenza Surveillance Report, week 5 ending 1 Feb 2025 (2024-25 season): 8.0% of emergency department visits had a discharge diagnosis of influenza (NSSP) and 7.8% of outpatient visits were for influenza-like illness against a 3.0% baseline, above baseline for the tenth consecutive week. If those visits are additional, arrivals rise by 1/(1-0.08) = 1.09.
arrival_multiplier.note: DERIVED: national peak-week share in a severe season, treated as additive. Diagnosed influenza undercounts attributable visits (Schanzer DL, Schwartz B, 2013, Acad Emerg Med 20(4):388-97: seasonal influenza about 500 ED visits per 100,000 population a year in Ontario, only 7% of them coded as influenza), so the true uplift may be higher; milder seasons are lower.

respiratory_share_uplift.citation: CDC ILINet weekly weighted percent of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness (wILI), HHS Region 2 (NJ, NY, PR, VI), obtained through the Delphi Epidata API mirror; 9 seasons 2014-15 to 2025-26 excluding 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22; mean excess of wILI over the off-season baseline during the wave weeks (as defined for duration_days), median across seasons, expressed as a share of visits
respiratory_share_uplift.note: PROXY: ILINet measures influenza-like illness as a share of OUTPATIENT-provider visits (it includes some EDs and urgent care), not the respiratory share of this hospital's ED arrivals. Peak-week excess median 0.0541; peak wILI is 4.39x the off-season baseline (range [3.18, 8.13]). Wave 0 placeholder was 0.12.

duration_days.citation: CDC ILINet weekly weighted percent of outpatient visits for influenza-like illness (wILI), HHS Region 2 (NJ, NY, PR, VI), obtained through the Delphi Epidata API mirror; 9 seasons 2014-15 to 2025-26 excluding 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22; per season, number of weeks with wILI at or above the off-season baseline (mean of weeks 21-39) plus half of the peak excess, x7; median across seasons
duration_days.note: Width of the wave at half its height; range = shortest to longest season. National median 77 days. Weeks above baseline + 2 SD (a looser definition) median 30 weeks. Per-season values: data/processed/fluview_ili_seasons.csv. Wave 0 placeholder was 42.
